subject: 2024 Medford Inauguration
overview: The City of Medford held its 2024 inauguration ceremony to swear in the Mayor, City Council, and School Committee for the new term. Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn delivered an inaugural address outlining major infrastructure goals, including a new high school, fire headquarters, and transit-oriented development.

items.title: Opening Ceremonies and Invocation
items.summary: The ceremony opened with the entrance of elected officials, the Pledge of Allegiance led by the Roberts Girls on the Run team, and an invocation by Rabbi Jessica Delera.

items.title: Poetry and Musical Performances
items.summary: Poet Laureate Vijaya Sundaram read 'Message from the Rooted World,' followed by Stacey Clayton performing 'God Bless America.'

items.title: Community Message
items.summary: Marie Cassidy of the Medford Family Network delivered a message on the importance of community support and building strong foundations for children and families.

items.title: Swearing-in of Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn
items.summary: State Representative Christine Barber introduced Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn, who was sworn in for her third term by her daughter, Calloway.

items.title: Inaugural Address
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn detailed plans for a new high school, a $25-30 million fire headquarters, and the development of 28 acres at Wellington Station. She emphasized the city's progress in affordable housing, climate resiliency grants, and the expansion of diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives in municipal hiring.

items.title: Oath of Office: City Council
items.summary: City Clerk Adam Hurtubise administered the oath of office to the seven members of the Medford City Council.

items.title: Musical Performance: Rise Up
items.summary: Stacey Clayton performed the song 'Rise Up' following the council's swearing-in.

items.title: Oath of Office: School Committee
items.summary: The six members of the Medford School Committee were sworn into office by City Clerk Adam Hurtubise.

items.title: Benediction and Closing
items.summary: Reverend Dr. David M. Kilpatrick offered a benediction for the city's leadership, followed by a final musical performance by the Medford Community Chorale.
